analysis: The question requires identifying which of the given options does not predispose to atherosclerosis. Homocystinemia (option opa) is known to contribute to atherosclerosis through endothelial damage caused by elevated homocysteine levels. Fibrinogen (option opb) promotes atherosclerosis by enhancing blood clotting and increasing the risk of thrombosis, which can lead to the development of atherosclerotic plaques. Lipoprotein A (option opd) is similar to LDL cholesterol and is directly involved in plaque formation, thus promoting atherosclerosis. In contrast, calcium (option opc) primarily deposits in arterial walls as a response to existing atherosclerotic damage rather than as a primary initiator of the disease. The role of calcium in atherosclerosis is more associated with influencing the stability of already formed plaques rather than initiating the formation of new plaques. Therefore, based on the consensus and the roles described, calcium is the correct answer as it does not directly predispose to the initiation of atherosclerosis.
